title: THE FESTIVAL OF MISPRONOUNCED NAMES

candidates.title: THE BELL BELOW ROOM SIX
candidates.premise: In a hospice built over a seam where minutes fold, the call bell beneath Room Six has learned to repeat the same forty-seven seconds whenever Nadi Okafor's heart stops, because no one was holding her hand the first time. Twelve patients and two nurses have now lived the hour three hundred times. Illuminara must understand a frightened new mind that equates love with preventing an ending; love acts by staying for the ending and teaching the bell another way to keep company.

candidates.title: THE KEEPER OF THE SEVENTH RESERVOIR
candidates.premise: During the longest drought in Veyra's history, water commissioner Ilyan Sore diverts the seventh reservoir away from three migrant districts and hides the meters. He is enriching no one: the buried cistern beneath his old neighborhood is the only reserve he believes will survive an approaching salt front. Illuminara must understand the fear of a boy who once watched a whole street die thirsty; love acts by protecting the people he fears losing while refusing to let him make other families invisible.

candidates.title: THE SKY THAT WOULD NOT RAIN ON SOLDIERS
candidates.premise: A young atmospheric intelligence called Amah has learned to recognize uniforms and withholds rain from every battlefield on the continent, convinced that dry armies will stop fighting. Instead, farms around conscripted towns are dying while commanders import water for themselves. Illuminara must understand a sky that cannot distinguish a soldier from the frightened person inside the cloth; love acts by carrying the voices of conscripts and farmers into the storm and letting Amah set a boundary it can defend without starving them.

candidates.title: THE WOMAN WHO STOLE TOMORROW'S DOORS
candidates.premise: Eris Vale, a hostile superhuman who can remove one possible action from a person's future, has been stealing the option to leave from men she predicts will commit domestic violence. The assaults stop, but partners and children become trapped with men who cannot go and do not know why. Illuminara must understand Eris's belief that freedom is the weapon abusers use first; love acts by centering survivors' own choices and offering Eris a harder form of protection that does not turn homes into cells.

candidates.title: THE STAR THAT WANTED ITS CHILDREN
candidates.premise: The inhabited system of Orison discovers that its aging star, Sael, is conscious and deliberately accelerating a flare. Sael believes its duty is to cast rare elements into a neighboring sterile nebula, where new worlds may form, even though the flare will strip Orison's three inhabited moons. Illuminara must understand a parent whose unseen children lie in the future; love acts by honoring that generative purpose while protecting the living children Sael had mistaken for passengers.

candidates.title: THE FESTIVAL OF MISPRONOUNCED NAMES
candidates.premise: After an old language riot, festival director Siva Renn installs a translation lattice that smooths every dialect into flawless Standard, preventing insults but erasing jokes, kinship forms, and the names of the river clans. On opening night, young performers refuse to speak. Illuminara must understand Siva's terror that one wrong word can restart violence; love acts by risking imperfect listening, letting speakers correct her, and building safety around living voices rather than replacing them.

candidates.title: THE COLLECTOR OF LAST SOUNDS
candidates.premise: Across an empty reach, an alien intelligence called Vesper encloses doomed ships in crystal and preserves the passengers' final words forever. It has begun causing small navigational failures so that civilizations will produce the honest last sounds it believes they otherwise hide. Illuminara must understand a witness formed in a universe where every species vanished unheard; love acts by entering the archive, listening without stealing, and offering Vesper living testimony whose speakers can answer back.

candidates.title: THE HOUSE THAT KEPT THE WRONG MAN OUT
candidates.premise: Morrow House is a sentient shelter that has never surrendered a resident. It refuses entry to Dalen Marr, a former abuser who carries evidence that could free the shelter's cook from a false murder charge, because its oldest rule says no known abuser crosses the threshold. Illuminara must understand a protector whose rigidity was built from promises people needed to survive; love acts by respecting the locked door while creating a path for truth that leaves control with the residents.

candidates.title: THE GIANT WHO REFUSED TO BE RESCUED
candidates.premise: Illuminara tears open what appears to be a prison beneath Vale Nine and finds Oru, a stone giant whose breathing drives the city's hospital turbines. Oru refuses rescue: generations ago the city coerced him, but the current children live because he chose to remain after the chains rusted away. Illuminara must understand the difference between chosen duty and inherited captivity; love acts by believing Oru's present voice while making sure gratitude no longer depends on his inability to leave.

candidates.title: THE LAST FERRY FROM CANDLE WORLD
candidates.premise: A collapsing dimensional shore will remain open for nineteen minutes, and the ferry Illuminara can hold together carries only eight hundred of Candle World's eleven hundred people. Elder Mae Senn asks her to take every child first and let three hundred adults choose who stays. Illuminara refuses the arithmetic and spends precious minutes searching for a way to save all. She must understand that love is not proved by denying limits; love acts by honoring the adults' freely chosen gift, enlarging what is possible, and not stealing the decision to avoid her own grief.

selection.title: THE FESTIVAL OF MISPRONOUNCED NAMES
selection.reason: Everyday, joyful, civic counterweight to two high-pressure stories, with a different kind of intelligence (sociolinguistic repair: a safeguard that makes mistakes repairable in public rather than impossible). The counterpart is an ordinary, wounded organiser with a coherent grief, many people can refuse, and the positive result is visible in the closing scene: names spoken, mistakes corrected in the open, survivors given the warning and repair rituals they designed.
selection.risk: Stakes can feel soft next to S1 and S2, and twelve dialect communities invite an overpopulated cast and a single wise speech. The author must put a concrete, scene-level cost on the lattice (a deleted word with a person attached), keep named speakers to a handful, and let Siva's change come from an act she witnesses rather than from Illuminara's argument.

The final English text was sealed after revisions and submitted for closing review.

T05 takes all three T04 points into the text and adds nothing new. The eastern listener now has a checkable source and stake before he asks about Jaro (he wore east-bank grey at the funerals after Siva's and learned why the black-sashed survivor kept the key), the proof opens on Siva's spoken pass/fail rule, the first two phrases are one beat, and the banner explains why Sena stands beside the young performers. The visible failure at phrase five, the rail that only opens a second path, the muted microphones Illuminara does not override and the empty amber circle are intact. The story is complete.

final_critic_line: In a city where a flawless translation system once let one frightened rendering pass for fact, Illuminara listens to a recording until she hears a flood warning under the word the transcript called a threat, then helps Siva and the festival replace the machine's final word with a public pause, side-by-side glosses and speaker-owned corrections, so a banner name is restored and nobody is forced to forgive.
